ramp.xds: Basic Setup

Source: R/xds_setup-info.R
xds_info_basic_setup.Rd

Basic Setup is defined by the use of xds_setup or one of its variants. It returns an xds model object that can be solved or or modified through advanced setup. The following briefly describes the modular design, the setup variants and when to use them, and a slightly longer discussion of what they do.

Modularity

ramp.xds is designed for modular computation. The mathematical framework has five core biological processes organized into three chunks called dynamical components (see xds_info_dynamical_components). The modular design makes it possible to study a system that with all three components fully defined (using xds_setup), or to develop systems of equations that isolate and study some part of a system.

To implement plug-and-play modularity, a trivial module was developed for each component. The trivial model ignores inputs from upstream modules, and it congfigures a a trace function to pass outputs downstream (see xds_info_trivial_forcing).

Basic Setup Functions

Depending on the purpose of the study, Basic Setup is done by one of five functions:

  • xds_setup can be used for most studies. It configures all three dynamical components.

  • xds_setup_human sets up an XH module to study disease dynamics forced by infective biting in the patches.

  • xds_setup_eir sets up an XH module to study disease dynamics forced by the daily EIR. Use this to study cohort dynamics using xds_solve_cohort.

  • xds_setup_mosy sets a model for mosquito ecology that ignores infection dynamics.

  • xds_setup_aquatic sets up a model for aquatic dynamics forced by egg laying.

Each function sets class(xds_obj$frame) to dispatch functions that are used to solve dynamical systems.

xds_setup

xds_setup sets class(xds_obj$frame)="full" and requires arguments to set up all three dynamical components.

xds_setup_mosy

xds_setup_mosy sets class(xds_obj$frame)="mosy" for models of mosquito ecology. It

  • sets up a L module

  • sets up a MY module, but the Y processes are ignored

  • sets up a trivial XH module to pass human population density

xds_setup_aquatic

xds_setup_aquatic sets class(xds_obj$frame)="aquatic"for models of aquatic mosquito ecology. It

  • sets up a L module

  • sets up a trivial MY module and configures a trace function for egg laying

  • sets up an XH component to be ignored

xds_setup_human

xds_setup_human sets class(xds_obj$frame)="human" for models of malaria epidemiology or other disease dynamics forced by infective biting in the patches. It

  • sets up the XH module

  • sets up a trivial MY component and configures a trace function for infective biting in patches

  • sets up an L component to be ignored

xds_setup_eir

xds_setup_eir sets class(xds_obj$frame)="eir" for models of malaria epidemiology or other disease dynamics forced by the EIR. These models can also be solved by xds_solve or xds_solve_cohort: in the former, time is the independent variable, and in the latter age. Unlike the other variants, these models lack the MY and L components. Instead, it

  • sets up the XH module

    • the average eir

    • a seasonal pattern function

    • a trend pattern function

    • a shock function

    • relative biting by age, which is used by xds_solve_cohort
